methodological_rigor.justification: A retrospective single-center cohort of 584 resected NSCLC patients was used to develop and internally validate five ML classifiers (LR, RF, XGBoost, SVM, NB) with an 8:2 train/test split and 5-fold CV on the training set, grid-search hyperparameter tuning, DeLong test for AUC comparison, calibration curves, Brier score, decision-curve analysis, and SHAP interpretation. These are appropriate methods. However, only 584 patients split 8:2 produces ~117 test samples with 44.4% STAS+, limiting precision; the authors explicitly exclude patients with missing data rather than imputing; no sample size justification is given. External validation is absent, and the final model is selected based on test-set AUC which can bias evaluation. The discrepancy between training (AUC 0.868) and test (AUC 0.764) suggests optimistic internal performance.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: As a retrospective single-center diagnostic/predictive modeling study, this maps to Oxford LoE 4. Clinical relevance is moderate because predicting STAS preoperatively could influence the choice between lobectomy and sub-lobar resection and lymph node dissection extent. The model uses only routinely available clinical and semantic CT features, improving accessibility compared to radiomics approaches, but without external validation or a prospective decision-impact study it cannot yet change practice.

reporting_quality.justification: TRIPOD is the appropriate standard for diagnostic/prognostic model development. The manuscript reports the study design, population, outcome definition (WHO 2021 STAS criteria, two blinded pathologists), predictors, handling of categorical/continuous variables, algorithms, hyperparameter tuning, calibration, discrimination, DCA, and model interpretability. TRIPOD is not explicitly cited, no checklist is appended, and items such as sample-size justification, missing-data handling (they simply exclude), and reporting of all candidate models are incomplete. Data availability is weak: no repository deposit of de-identified data or code URLs are stated (the scikit-learn/XGBoost URLs are [REDACTED]).

novelty_literature.justification: XGBoost + SHAP for preoperative STAS prediction has been published very recently (ref 31 Wang P et al., Acad Radiol 2025) and multiple radiomics-based STAS predictors exist (refs 8, 9, 29, 35, 40). The authors' novelty claim is that their model uses only clinical and semantic CT features (no radiomics) and covers NSCLC rather than only adenocarcinoma, which is a meaningful incremental contribution for deployability but not a paradigm shift. Guarded against leniency, novelty is incremental.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is clearly organized with explicit baseline characteristics, algorithm descriptions, and a structured Results section covering model performance (ROC, calibration, Brier, DCA, Taylor diagram) and SHAP-based interpretation. Figures are referenced systematically. Minor rough edges include redundant phrasing ('the present study'), inconsistency around the T stage labelling (methods mention T0/T1/T2 but results include T3 stage), and [REDACTED] placeholders for code URLs.

key_strengths: Uses only routinely available clinical and semantic CT features (no radiomics), improving deployability in resource-limited settings
Comprehensive model comparison across five algorithms with DeLong test, calibration curves, Brier scores, DCA, and Taylor diagram
SHAP-based interpretability with reasonable top predictors (nodule type, lobulation, smoking) that align with biological plausibility
Outcome definition follows 2021 WHO STAS criteria with two blinded pulmonary pathologists
key_concerns: Single-center retrospective design without external validation limits generalizability
Patients with missing data were excluded rather than imputed, potentially introducing selection bias
Test-set performance (AUC 0.764) is notably lower than training (AUC 0.868), and model selection was partially based on test-set AUC
Novelty is incremental relative to recent XGBoost+SHAP STAS prediction work in lung adenocarcinoma
No data/code deposition; inconsistencies in T-stage coding (methods: T0/T1/T2; results: T1/T2/T3)
chief_reviewer.rationale: A competent single-center ML prediction study for STAS using routinely available features, appropriate for a mid-tier specialty oncology or thoracic-imaging journal with minor revisions to add external validation plans, clarify inconsistencies, and deposit data/code.
